questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down, then pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: What should you wear to help other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothes to be more visible to other drivers. This helps you be seen both during the day and at night.

questions.question: Which is NOT something your lane position should do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen, helps you avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast you drank the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: How often you drink alcohol.
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol you consumed, how fast you consumed it, and your body weight. Your sex, physical condition, and food intake can also have some effect.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding, what happens to the steering?
questions.correctAnswerText: It becomes hard to turn.
questions.explanation: If the front tire fails, the steering becomes hard to turn. If you feel heavy steering, pull off the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To estimate remaining drinks, subtract the number of hours since drinking from the total drinks consumed. In this case: 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals 4 drinks remaining.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle should:

options.text: Let you touch the ground with your feet while sitting on the seat.
Have a seat at the same height as your waist.
Have a seat 10 inches above your waist.
Have a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let you touch the ground with your feet while sitting on the seat.
questions.explanation: Your feet should reach the ground while you are seated. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: When a group passes another vehicle, what is the best way?

options.text: One rider passes completely before the next rider starts to pass.
Several riders pass the vehicle at the same time.
The last rider waves to show no more motorcycles are coming.
Riders pass in a staggered line.

questions.correctAnswerText: One rider passes completely before the next rider starts to pass.
questions.explanation: Group riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish their pass and return to formation before the next rider begins to pass.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down, then pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Slow down with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear safely.
Speed up before shifting to a lower gear safely.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear safely.
questions.explanation: Before shifting to a lower gear, make sure you are going slow enough to shift safely. Shifting too fast can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to skid. When going downhill or shifting into first gear, use your brakes to slow down to a safe speed first.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your whole head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look at where you want to go by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced while turning. Your arms should be slightly bent when you hold the handgrips.

questions.question: What is often used on roads to direct riders into the correct lanes for turning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Painted white arrows
questions.explanation: White arrows painted on the pavement tell you which direction to travel from that lane. Follow the arrows along with any signs or traffic signals.

questions.question: What color is a sign that warns you about a hazard ahead?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black letters
questions.explanation: Warning signs about hazards are yellow with black letters and symbols. Always pay attention to these warning signs.

questions.question: What percent of motorcycle-and-car crashes are caused by the driver failing to yield the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-and-car crashes happen because the driver does not yield the right-of-way to the rider.

questions.question: When does alcohol impairment start?
questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the legal limit
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Alcohol impairs your riding ability well before you reach the legal limit.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass
Use your horn and make rude gestures
Speed up to create distance between you

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass if you can. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group
At the back of the group

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders at the back can watch them.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit
Shift into neutral when slowing down

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces your reaction time if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases you?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If chased, downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes
Press the front brake hard to prevent the tire from locking
Use only one brake at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake lever gently and use light pressure on the rear brake to avoid locking the wheels.
